answer: Picture a ledge where every new account waits one full epoch before it can grade or earn. During that wait the network compares its join time, funding source and first answers with others who arrived in the same burst. Accounts that land within minutes of each other, like quartz grains washed down one ridge, count as a single cohort sharing one grading seat and one reward slot until their behaviour diverges. A farm that spins up 500 clones overnight earns as one, so it must spread joins over weeks and pay the admission work every time.
